notes: Overview: LumenFlow is a mid-market SaaS (B2B) that provides a multi-tenant conversational agent platform embedded in partner apps. Heavy chat/agent traffic during business hours; bursty spikes from onboarding windows.

Current evaluation path: started with Hosted API (fast onboarding) -> demo on 2026-01-28 -> small POC in Hosted -> ran latency+streaming tests -> now weighing Dedicated (predictable throughput, per-tenant isolation) for 2026 Q3 rollout.
Key quote from CTO (02/25): 'We need streaming to not drop inside long-running tool calls — losing a single token leads to agent state drift.'

POC details: 2-week test in hosted environment simulating 3k concurrent sessions (avg 250ms target p50), tool-calling chains up to 4 external tools, KV cache usage for context. Observed p50=210ms baseline, p95 spiked to 1.2s during a simulated onboarding burst.
Streaming notes: some reconnects on websockets at 60–90s under load; suspect batching/backpressure interplay. SE reproduced with local runner (see RDW-1124) and shared traces.
Rate limiting: product requires per-tenant quotas + soft throttles and clear 429 semantics. Want tenant-level cost billing and predictable SLA per customer tier.
Security: must pass SSO/SAML integration, SOC2 ok to rely on Redwood SOC2 + audit logs + KMS for key management. Data residency: US-only for enterprise customers.

Commercial: procurement prefers committed Dedicated pricing for 12 months to get unit discounts. Finance asked for usage delta scenarios (hosted vs dedicated) before committing. Target ARR band $80k-150k depending on committed nodes.
Stability ask: demo a fallback routing policy (hosted -> dedicated variant) during simulated capacity loss; show streaming failover and no-duplicate-events guarantees.
Docs/Artifacts: security questionnaire submitted (drive:security/faq-lumenflow-review-2026-02.md), demo recording (fireflies ff_9f2b7c_call_2026-02-12), POC traces attached in Jira RDW-1124.
